plan.title: Paired 3-condition blood RNA-seq: treatment A/B vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000 x 13 gene-level count table from Salmon (counts.csv) plus a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv) with subject and condition: 4 human blood donors, each contributing a control, a treated_a and a treated_b sample (12 samples, single batch). The research question has two parts — which genes respond to either treatment within a subject, and whether the two treatments differ — and the paired three-level design answers both with one model.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC on the raw counts: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition and by subject. With n=4 subjects the dominant axis of variance is expected to be the donor, and the QC exists to confirm the pairing is real and to spot a sample that does not sit with its donor before any test runs.

T1S2 fits the count model. Genes are pre-filtered minimally (>=10 counts in at least 4 samples, the smallest group size), size factors are median-of-ratios estimated inside DESeq2 (no pre-scaling of the counts). The design is ~ subject + condition, which removes the between-donor variation so every comparison is made within a donor. Part one of the question is the likelihood ratio test of the full design ~ subject + condition against the reduced ~ subject: this is the 'responds to either treatment' gene set, since it flags any gene that differs across the three conditions within subjects. Part two is served by three named Wald contrasts with control as the explicit reference level: treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, and treated_b vs treated_a. The last is a contrast between two non-reference levels, so log2 fold changes are shrunk with ashr (apeglm cannot take a contrast), and both the shrunken and unshrunken estimates are reported. BH adjustment is applied within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on.

A data caveat drives one constraint: the counts are gene-level output from Salmon as delivered, and the profile does not state whether a length correction was applied. No per-sample quant.sf and no average transcript length table are present, so the model is fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and both the fold-change table and the report must state that the length offset is lost — a change in isoform usage can therefore surface as differential expression. tximport is not run on a gene-level table.

T2S1 takes the interpretation step: preranked fgsea per contrast on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (chosen over signed p-value, which ties, and over the fold change alone, which is noisy at low counts) against the human MSigDB hallmark sets, then Reactome and WikiPathways as further collections, each tested separately with its release stated. The LRT gene set is small enough at n=4 that an over-representation test on it would be underpowered; the ranked test on the full tested list is the method that survives the sample size.

T1S3 assembles the report with the MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, per-contrast counts, leading-edge genes, and the reproducibility record. Power is the honest limit here: 4 subjects per condition is at the low end, and the pairing is the only reason the design has any sensitivity at all.

constraints: Use the full ranked list of tested genes; never a list thresholded by padj or fold change
Rank by the Wald statistic (stat), not by unshrunken log2 fold change alone and not by a signed p-value
min set size 15, max set size 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Run enrichment once per contrast; never pool genes from different contrasts into one list
Use human gene sets only — the environment also holds mouse and rat collections and those must not be used here
State the release/version of every gene set collection used
Set and record the random seed for the permutation-based p-values
caveats: If fewer than about 50 genes pass padj<0.05 in a contrast, do not fall back to an over-representation test on that short list — the ranked test on the full list is the method; state the size of the significant list either way
Enrichment results depend on the method and the collection; present hits as hypotheses for follow-up, not as established findings
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment on count data; state the universe (the tested genes) in the report

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea per contrast on the full tested list per R-0107@976c, human Hallmark first then Reactome and WikiPathways per R-0048@500d and R-0165@e456. Disputed rule R-0108@409f: the Wald statistic (stat) is the chosen ranking metric, because it is signed and scaled by its standard error and does not tie the way a signed p-value does at n=4.

steps.name: Integrated report
steps.question: What is the consolidated answer: which genes respond to either treatment within subject, how do treated_a and treated_b differ from each other and from control, and what processes do those changes implicate — with what confidence at n=4?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from the T1S2 model output and the T2S1 enrichment output. Include: the design formula ~ subject + condition with control as the stated reference level; the three named contrasts; the number of genes tested after filtering (out of 12,000) and the number significant per contrast plus the LRT; the MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics, placed before the gene tables; the p-value histograms; a gene table per contrast carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value; a summary of how the treated_a and treated_b response sets overlap and where the two treatments diverge (the treated_b vs treated_a contrast); the per-collection enrichment tables with rank metric, universe, size window, collection name and release; the leading-edge genes of each reported set. Close with the limitations: 4 subjects per condition, gene-level Salmon counts used with no length offset (isoform-usage shifts can masquerade as differential expression), FDR controlled within each contrast and not across the three, and enrichment hits stated as method-dependent hypotheses. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed used for the permutation tests, and the gene set collection releases.
steps.context: Final synthesis for the paired 3-condition blood RNA-seq study of 4 subjects. The two-part research question maps directly onto two outputs: the LRT table answers 'responds to either treatment within subject', and the treated_b vs treated_a contrast answers 'do the treatments differ from each other'. Both must be presented with the sample-size limitation stated plainly rather than buried.
acceptance_criteria: Report names the method, package versions, design formula, reference level, all three contrasts, thresholds, number of genes tested and number of DE genes per contrast and for the LRT
MA plot and dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, each with a caption saying what it shows
Gene tables carry both the unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold change with lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value
Overlap between the treated_a and treated_b response gene sets is quantified, and genes significant in treated_b vs treated_a are listed separately
Enrichment section states the collection, its release, the rank metric, the universe and the size window, and lists leading-edge genes per reported set
Limitations section explicitly states the n=4 power limit, the missing length offset, and that FDR is per-contrast not across contrasts
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package versions, collection releases) is stored with the results
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the contrast name beside every adjusted p-value and every gene list
Do not present the union of contrasts as a single result set
State the enrichment method dependence explicitly
caveats: No second differential-expression method is run in this plan, so no two-method overlap statistic is available; say so rather than implying robustness that was not tested
At 4 subjects, absence of significance is weak evidence of absence of effect

grounding.reason: No rule selects the report step as a method; its contents follow the reporting claims cited (diagnostics, effect columns, enrichment reporting, reproducibility record). The two-method overlap of R-0042@54e1 is not applicable because only DESeq2 is run, and the report states that.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
